To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed affine MMSE-PATS achieve the optimal pilot/data power allocation and are the optimal PAT schemes in the sense of minimizing the mean squared error of the channel estimate.

1) the channel's spreading properties should be taken into consideration when choosing among affine PAT schemes, 2) multicarrier MMSEPAT achieves higher ergodic achievable rates than single-carriers MMSEPAT when the channel delay-spread dominates the Doppler-spread and vice-versa, and 3) a pilot/data power allocation scheme is developed that is optimal for affine MMSE-PAt schemes

(a) multicarrier MMSEPAT is preferable to single-carrier MMSEPAT when the channel is highly dispersive and (b) single-carrier MMSEC-PAT is preferable to multicarrier MMSEC-PAt when the channel is frequency-flat and/or the number of transmit antennas is large
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of MMSE-PAT systems over doubly-selective channels, and provides a complete analysis of the ergodically achievable rate of such schemes
the design, analysis, and optimization of PAT schemes that are capable of achieving the highest possible rates over doubly selective channels.
the design and performance analysis of MMSE-PAT over doubly selective channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for affine MMSE PAT schemes, the choice of the spreading parameters should be made in accordance with the relative strength of the delay-spread and Doppler-spread of the channel, and that the choice of the pilot/data pattern should be made in a manner that minimizes the MSE.
multicarrier PAT is preferred when the delay-spread dominates the Doppler-spread of the channel, and vice versa for single-carrier PAT.

, for the single-antennas, doubly selective channel, the proposed affine MMSE-PATH scheme achieves the best tradeoff between the achievable rates and the channel estimation MSE, and the pilot/data power allocation can further enhance the performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

affine cyclic-prefix MMSE-PAT provides a simple yet efficient solution to the design and analysis of pilot-aid channel estimation for the doubly selective channel, which can serve as a benchmark for more complex schemes.

, when compared to existing schemes, the proposed affine MMSE-Pat schemes are capable of achieving higher rates at low-to-moderate SNRs, and are capable of achieving lower error probabilities at high SNRs.

the channel's delay- and Doppler-spreads should both be taken into account in the design of MMSE-PAT, and that multicarrier PAT is more suitable for channels whose delay-spread is larger than their Doppler-spread.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the channel spreading parameters can be used to improve PAT's ergodic achievable rates, and that multicarrier PAT should be considered when the channel's Doppler-spread is negligible.
the channel's spread parameters play a crucial role in the design of MMSE-PAT.
the channel's delay/Doppler-spreading parameters should be taken as design parameters when choosing among affine cyclic-prefix MMSE-PAT transmission schemes.
